messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

output:
You didn't name the service, the platform, or the dates, so I've written it with bracketed placeholders you can fill in. Swap them and it's ready to send.

---

**Subject: [Service] moves to [New Platform] in [Q_ 20__]**

Hi [Name],

We're moving [Service] to [New Platform] next quarter. Here's what that means for you.

The short version: your account, your data, and your saved [settings/reports/workflows] come with you. You don't need to export anything or rebuild your setup. We're handling the migration on our side.

Why we're doing it. [Old Platform] has been running [Service] since [year], and it's reached the end of what we can do with it — [specific limitation, e.g. "batch jobs cap out at 500 records" or "no support for SSO"]. [New Platform] fixes that. It also gets you [specific gain: faster exports, an API, whatever is true].

The dates:
- [Date] — new URL goes live. Both platforms work. Log in with your existing credentials.
- [Date] — we migrate remaining accounts in batches. You'll get 48 hours' notice by email before yours moves.
- [Date] — [Old Platform] switches to read-only.
- [Date] — [Old Platform] shuts down.

What we need from you. Two things, and only if they apply. If you've hardcoded [old-domain.com] into scripts or integrations, update them to [new-domain.com] before [date]. If your team uses [feature that isn't carrying over], talk to us — we'll work out a replacement.

Expect one short outage during your migration window, under [X] minutes.

Questions go to [email] or [support link]. We'd rather hear from you early than fix something after.

— [Name], [Title]
